title: Long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax on listed equity
body:
Gains on listed equity shares and equity mutual fund units held for more than 12 months are long-term capital gains.

From 23 July 2024, LTCG under section 112A is taxed at 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh in a financial year. The exemption limit was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹1.25 lakh by the Union Budget 2024.

Indexation benefit is not available for listed equity LTCG. Securities transaction tax must have been paid for section 112A to apply.

title: Short-term capital gains (STCG) tax on listed equity
body:
Gains on listed equity shares held for 12 months or less are short-term capital gains.

From 23 July 2024, STCG under section 111A is taxed at 20%, up from 15%. Surcharge and cess apply on top of the base rate.

title: T+1 settlement cycle
body:
Indian equity markets moved fully to the T+1 settlement cycle on 27 January 2023. Shares bought on trading day T are credited to the demat account, and sale proceeds are paid, on the next working day.

SEBI also introduced an optional same-day (T+0) settlement for a limited set of stocks in March 2024.

title: Market-wide circuit breakers
body:
Market-wide circuit breakers halt trading on all equity and derivative segments when the NIFTY 50 or the Sensex moves 10%, 15% or 20% from the previous close.

The length of the halt depends on the threshold and the time of day. A 20% move halts trading for the rest of the day.

Individual stocks also have price bands, typically 2%, 5%, 10% or 20%, beyond which orders are not accepted.

title: XIRR (extended internal rate of return)
body:
XIRR is the annualised return of a series of cash flows that happen on irregular dates, such as SIP instalments, top-ups and partial sales.

It is the discount rate at which the net present value of all cash flows, including the current portfolio value as a final inflow, equals zero.

XIRR is more meaningful than absolute return when money was invested at different times. Arth computes XIRR from your recorded transactions and today's value.

title: Price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio
body:
The price-to-earnings ratio is the share price divided by earnings per share over the last twelve months.

It shows how many rupees investors pay for one rupee of annual profit. A P/E is only comparable within a sector, because growth and capital intensity differ widely between sectors.

A high P/E is not by itself a sign that a stock is overvalued, and a low P/E is not by itself a sign that it is cheap.

title: Market capitalisation buckets (large, mid, small cap)
body:
AMFI classifies listed companies by full market capitalisation every six months. The top 100 companies are large cap, companies ranked 101 to 250 are mid cap, and companies ranked 251 and below are small cap.

Arth uses these buckets for the allocation by market cap view.

title: NIFTY 50 index and ETF proxies
body:
The NIFTY 50 is a free-float market capitalisation weighted index of 50 large Indian companies listed on the NSE.

Index values cannot be bought directly. Arth compares portfolios against NIFTYBEES, an exchange-traded fund that tracks the NIFTY 50, as a tradable proxy. ETF prices can differ slightly from the index because of tracking error and expense ratio.

title: Dividends and their taxation
body:
Since 1 April 2020, dividends are taxable in the hands of the shareholder at their income tax slab rate.

Companies deduct TDS of 10% when dividends paid to a resident individual exceed ₹5,000 in a financial year.

title: Diversification and concentration
body:
Concentration describes how much of a portfolio sits in a single stock or sector. A portfolio where one holding is a large share of the total value moves closely with that holding.

Diversification spreads value across holdings and sectors whose prices do not move together. Arth reports allocation by sector, market cap bucket and asset class so you can see concentration; it does not tell you what to change.

title: SEBI registered investment advisers
body:
Under the SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013, only SEBI-registered investment advisers may give personalised advice on buying, selling or holding securities for a fee.

Arth is an information tool. It describes your portfolio and public information and does not recommend buying, selling or holding any security.
